correctness.rationale: The primary extremizer has 3n-1 distinct nonsingular anti-rational zeros, with n orientation-preserving and 2n-1 orientation-reversing. For the logharmonic equation F=p conjugate(H), differentiation at a root gives J_F=-|p|^2 J_H, hence the split becomes 2n-1 positive and n negative. The real-analytic implicit-function theorem continues all roots under arbitrary small coefficient perturbations, while the general 3n-1 upper bound prevents any additional roots. This proves exact persistence of maximal valence and the orientation counts.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A general implicit-function theorem alone only preserves existing simple roots locally; it does not rule out extra roots appearing elsewhere. The logharmonic global upper bound is therefore an essential domain-specific ingredient in the exact maximal-valence conclusion.

value.rationale: The sharpness theorem is existential, so whether maximal valence is robust or fine-tuned is mathematically substantive. The finding proves a full-dimensional open extremal locus at a fixed target and preserves the complete Jacobian-sign profile. This is stronger than the source one-parameter openness and the older fixed-map target stability, and it provides a reusable perturbative description of generic maximal-valence behavior.
